##

```{r}

# Connect to the DuckDB database
# Replace 'path/to/your/database.duckdb' with your actual database path
con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "/workspaces/reports/data/ResStock/2022_resstock_amy2018_release_1.1/rs_20250307_37M.db")


# Query the database for January data
# Filter for month = 1 (January)
query <- "
SELECT
  COUNT(bldg_id) as count
FROM
  hourly_2022
WHERE
  month = 1
"

# Execute the query
january_data <- dbGetQuery(con, query)

# Disconnect from the database
dbDisconnect(con)

# Calculate mean energy consumption by day and hour
daily_hourly_mean <- january_data %>%
  group_by(day, hour) %>%
  summarize(mean_energy = mean(energy, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

# Create a datetime variable for proper plotting
daily_hourly_mean <- daily_hourly_mean %>%
  mutate(datetime = ymd_h(paste0("2025-01-", day, " ", hour)))


# Create the plot
energy_plot <- ggplot(daily_hourly_mean, aes(x = datetime, y = mean_energy)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2C7FB8", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#2C7FB8", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Home Energy Consumption in January",
    subtitle = "Hourly average across all buildings",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Mean Energy Consumption",
    caption = "Data source: DuckDB database with 262M rows"
  ) +
  scale_x_datetime(
    date_labels = "%d %b %H:00",
    date_breaks = "3 days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(energy_plot)





```
